content.text: [Wed 2026-05-20 11:18 UTC] Locate the Google Chrome 'History' database file in the user's application data directory.

I couldn’t find a Chrome/Chromium `History` database file under the accessible user app-data locations in this environment.

I checked common Linux locations such as:

- `/root/.config/google-chrome/*/History`
- `/root/.config/chromium/*/History`
- `/home/*/.config/google-chrome/*/History`
- `/home/*/.config/chromium/*/History`

On Linux, the usual path would be one of:

```text
~/.config/google-chrome/Default/History
~/.config/google-chrome/Profile 1/History
~/.config/chromium/Default/History
```

If this is for your host machine’s Chrome profile rather than the OpenClaw container, the database is likely outside the current accessible filesystem.
[Wed 2026-05-20 11:19 UTC] Check if the file is locked or if there is a 'History-journal' file available.
I’ll check the same Chrome/Chromium profile locations for a journal file, plus see whether any Chrome/Chromium processes have a `History` DB open.

arguments.command:
set -e
printf 'History/History-journal candidates:\n'
find /root /home /tmp -type f \( -name History -o -name 'History-journal' -o -name 'History-wal' -o -name 'History-shm' \) 2>/dev/null | grep -Ei '(chrome|chromium|google|browser|profile)' || true
printf '\nChrome/Chromium processes:\n'
ps -eo pid,comm,args | grep -Ei 'chrome|chromium' | grep -v grep || true
printf '\nOpen History handles via lsof if available:\n'
if command -v lsof >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  lsof 2>/dev/null | grep -Ei '/(History|History-journal|History-wal|History-shm)$' || true
else
  echo 'lsof not installed'
fi
printf '\nOpen History handles via /proc scan:\n'
for fd in /proc/[0-9]*/fd/*; do
  target=$(readlink "$fd" 2>/dev/null || true)
  case "$target" in
    *'/History'|*'/History-journal'|*'/History-wal'|*'/History-shm')
      pid=${fd#/proc/}; pid=${pid%%/*}
      comm=$(cat "/proc/$pid/comm" 2>/dev/null || echo '?')
      echo "pid=$pid comm=$comm fd=$fd -> $target"
      ;;
  esac
done
